title: IaC Best Practices
description: Apply infrastructure as code best practices for modular design, state management, secret handling, and CI/CD.

data.text: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) is powerful, but it requires discipline. Following best practices ensures your infrastructure is maintainable, secure, and scalable as your team and environment grow.

items.text: Use modular design — group related resources together
Store state remotely with locking (e.g., S3 + DynamoDB for Terraform)
Never hardcode secrets — use AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store
Use consistent naming conventions for resources
Tag all resources for cost tracking and organization
Run linting and validation in CI/CD (e.g., tflint, cfn-lint)
Apply least-privilege IAM for IaC execution roles
Version control all IaC code in Git

data.text: Testing IaC catches errors before they reach production. You can use **Terratest** for Terraform, **cfn-lint** for CloudFormation, and **AWS CDK assertions** for CDK. Write tests for security, naming, and cost.

data.title: CI/CD Pipeline Stages
items: **Plan** — preview changes (Terraform plan, CloudFormation change set)
**Apply** — deploy changes with manual approval for production
**Notify** — alert the team of success or failure

data.title: Key Principle
data.text: Treat infrastructure code the same as application code: review it, test it, and deploy it through automated pipelines.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Design IaC in modules for reusability and maintainability
Remote state and locking are essential for team collaboration
Never store secrets in code — use dedicated secret managers
Automate testing and deployment through CI/CD
